questions.q: Why are attention scores divided by the square root of the head size?
options: To make the softmax saturate faster
To keep the softmax from saturating as vectors get longer
To reduce the number of parameters
To sort the tokens by position
questions.explain: Dot products grow with vector length; scaling keeps scores in a range where the softmax still gives useful, non-saturated weights.

questions.q: In the lesson's shuffle test without positional encodings, what happened when the input tokens were shuffled?
options: The output changed completely
The model raised an error
The output was simply shuffled the same way (difference about 1e-15)
The output became all zeros
questions.explain: Attention treats its input as a set, so without positional information word order is invisible to the block.

questions.q: What does the causal mask do in a text-generating Transformer?
options: Prevents each position from attending to later positions
Removes stop words from the input
Randomly drops half of the heads
Converts tokens to lowercase
questions.explain: The mask sets scores for future positions to a huge negative number, so their softmax weights become zero and each token is predicted only from earlier ones.

questions.q: What is the role of a residual connection in a Transformer block?
options: It replaces the attention weights with zeros
It converts the vectors to integers
It doubles the sequence length
It adds the sublayer's input back to its output so deep stacks stay trainable
questions.explain: Adding the input to the output gives gradients a short path through the network, which is a key reason many blocks can be stacked.

questions.q: Roughly where do most of the parameters of a standard Transformer block sit?
options: In the attention projections and the feed-forward layer, about 12 times d squared together
In the softmax, which has one weight per token
In the positional encodings, which are learned matrices in every model
In the causal mask
questions.explain: Four d-by-d matrices for attention plus two d-by-4d matrices for the feed-forward layer come to about 12 d squared per block.
